intentAndPurpose.intent: Primary HeaderWeb row. Figma publishes homeBar, contextBar, and searchBar types with fluid or centered middle content.

props.name: activeValue
props.description: Active nav item value — used to position the sliding indicator

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for the primary navigation landmark. Defaults to "Primary navigation". Override when rendering multiple `PrimaryNav` instances on the same page so each `<nav>` is uniquely labelled.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: IDREF of a visible element that labels the navigation landmark.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar element for far-end

props.name: children
props.description: Nav items for middle section (HeaderItem components)

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name

props.name: divider
props.description: Show/hide bottom divider. Default: true

props.name: end
props.description: End slot content (icon actions before avatar)

props.name: logo
props.description: Logo element for start slot

props.name: middle
props.type: /** * Collapses the middle region entirely (`display: none`). Code-only * extension — the Figma set exposes just `fluid | centered` and models an * empty middle by omitting its content. Retained because contextBar-style * headers need an explicit way to reclaim the space. */ | 'none' | 'fluid' | 'centered' /** @deprecated Use the Figma-canonical `centered` spelling. */ | 'centred'
props.description: Middle section layout: fluid (fills space) or centered (absolute center)

props.description: Forwarded to the embedded `SearchInput`'s `aria-labelledby`.

props.description: Where search input appears: none (hidden), middle (with nav items), end (in actions area)

props.description: Search value (controlled)

props.name: showAvatar
props.description: Show/hide avatar. Default: true

props.name: showMenuButton
props.description: Show hamburger menu icon button in the leading chrome section.

props.name: startActions

props.name: title
props.description: Context-bar title rendered after the leading action.

props.description: Bar type: homeBar (nav items), contextBar (simpler), searchBar (search-focused)

interactionBehavior.summary: PrimaryNav is a `<nav>` landmark whose items are ordinary sequential Tab stops — there is no arrow-key roving. Child HeaderItems default to `attention="low"` (this row does not pass an attention into selection context), so the current item is high-emphasis text only, not a pill. On mobile/tablet (`data-breakpoint` S or M) the hamburger IconButton is the way into the drawer; the middle item row is `display: none` at S, and search is hidden until L.
hover: The row itself has no hover fill. Child HeaderItems own pointer chrome — and at this row's default `attention="low"` that chrome is a text-colour shift, not a background (see HeaderItem).
The leading control is an IconButton (`icon="menu"`, `attention="low"`, `appearance="neutral"`), so its hover is IconButton's ghost treatment, `(hover: hover)`-guarded.
press: Clicking a child HeaderItem calls `onActiveValueChange` with that item's `value` unless the item `preventDefault`s.

The hamburger IconButton calls `onDrawerOpenChange(true)` — the header's own setter when nested, or the PrimaryNav prop when provided — and is a no-op unless a `WebHeader.Drawer` (or a consumer) actually reads that state.
focus: The `<nav>` is not focusable. Tab order is sequential through the hamburger (when shown), each HeaderItem, the search field (when shown), and the `end` / avatar slots.
There is no roving `tabIndex` — every HeaderItem stays in the tab order at once, unlike BottomNavigation.
keyboard: No arrow-key handler. `Enter` / `Space` activate whichever HeaderItem or IconButton is focused, using those primitives' own keys.
Search is the shared `<Search>` (`clearable={false}`); `Enter` in the field fires `onSearchSubmit`.
Responsive CSS is scoped to a `.webHeader[data-breakpoint]` ancestor, so a standalone PrimaryNav (no WebHeader) keeps the middle row and hamburger visible regardless of viewport.
selected: `activeValue` / `onActiveValueChange` on this row drive child HeaderItems through `HeaderSelectionContext`. An item's explicit `active={false}` still wins over a matching parent `activeValue`.
Because this row does not pass `attention`, children resolve to `attention="low"`: the current item is `aria-current="page"` with `--Neutral-High` text and neither a pill nor the medium underline.
That is the opposite of SecondaryNav, whose default `attention="high"` paints a `--Primary-Subtle` pill on the current item.
touch: At breakpoint S the middle HeaderItems are not in the layout (`display: none`), so they are not a touch target; the hamburger is the navigation affordance and opens `WebHeader.Drawer`.
At M the middle items return and the hamburger stays visible. Search remains hidden until L (`≥ 991px`).
